rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: the queen on e4 and the rook on a5 attack both your rooks, but it is your move. The black king is on e8, on the edge, and your rook on a7 closes the seventh rank.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.p: With the seventh rank closed, find the move of the other rook that gives mate.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes, it is mate: the rook on b1 checks on b8, along the eighth rank, and the one on a7 takes every square of the seventh from the king.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.revela: The rook on b1 goes to b8 and gives mate: the check comes along the eighth rank, and the rook on a7 takes the seventh-rank squares from the king.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.err.a7a8.1: The rook checks on a8, but it leaves the seventh rank and lands on the diagonal of the queen on e4.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.err.a7a8.2: With this move Black has a resource: the queen captures the rook, and the one on b1 is left alone.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.err.a7a8.3: Back to the position: leave the rook on a7 on the seventh and give check with the other one.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.err.a7a5.1: The rook captures the one on a5, but it leaves the seventh rank and leaves the one on b1 attacked by the queen.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.err.a7a5.2: With this move Black has a resource: the queen captures the rook on b1 with mate, because your king is also trapped behind its pawns.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.err.a7a5.3: Back to the position: before capturing, look for the check with the rook on b1.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not give mate, and Black gains time for its own attack. Look for the check with the rook on b1 on the eighth rank.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: the rook on a7 closes the seventh; look for the check on the eighth.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.l1: This is the ladder: two rooks, or queen and rook, on neighbouring ranks. One closes the rank in front, and the other checks on the edge. With the king on the edge file, the same works with files.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex1.l2: Here the king was already on the edge, and one check was enough. Before it, check that no black piece can capture the checking rook.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: the black king is on b8, behind the pawns on a7 and b6, and your pawn on a6 has come close to it. Black threatens your king with the rooks and the queen.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.p: Find the queen move that gives mate.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.certo: Yes, it is mate: the queen checks on b7, next to the king, and the pawn on a6 supports it. The king cannot capture it.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.revela: The queen goes to b7 and gives mate: it stands next to the king, supported by the pawn on a6, and covers a8, c8 and c7.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.err.e4a8.1: The queen checks on a8, next to the king, but none of your pieces supports that square.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.err.e4a8.2: With this move Black has a resource: the king captures the queen, because it had no support.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.err.e4a8.3: Back to the position: look for the square next to the king that one of your pieces supports.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.err.e4f4.1: The queen goes to f4 without check, far from the black king.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.err.e4f4.2: With this move Black has a resource: the pawn on g5 attacks your queen, and Black gains time for its own attack.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.err.e4f4.3: Back to the position: look for the queen check next to the king, with support.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.err.e4e5.1: The queen captures the rook on e5 with check, but the black queen on e6 defends that square.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.err.e4e5.2: With this move Black has a resource: the queen on e6 recaptures, and you are left without your queen.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.err.e4e5.3: Back to the position: look for the check next to the king, with support.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not give mate, and Black has time to attack your king. Look for the square next to the black king that one of your pieces supports.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the queen check next to the king, with support.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.l1: This is the supported queen: next to the king, it covers the squares around it, and the support stops the king from capturing it. Here the support is a pawn; it can be a piece or your king.
rot.queenRookMates.ideia.ex2.l2: In positions like this, before the check next to the king, check the support: without it, the king captures the queen.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.bispo.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side. The white king is on g1, and your bishop on h3 watches f1 and g2, next to it.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.bispo.p: Find the queen check, supported by the bishop, that gives mate.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.bispo.certo: Yes, it is mate: the queen checks on f1, next to the king, and the bishop on h3 supports it.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.bispo.revela: The queen goes to f1 and gives mate: it stands next to the king, supported by the bishop on h3.
The queen checks on g2, supported by the bishop, but the rook on e2 also reaches that square.
With this move White has a resource: the rook captures the queen, and the bishop only gets the rook back.
Back to the position: look for the square next to the king that only the king defends.
The queen checks on g4, along the g-file, but far from the king: it has squares to escape to.
With this move White has a resource: the king escapes to f2, and White, with extra pieces, defends.
Back to the position: look for the square next to the king that your bishop supports.
The queen checks on f2, but without support: the rook on e2, the queen on d4 and the king defend that square.
With this move White has a resource: the queen on d4 captures yours, and the attack is over.
Back to the position: look for the square next to the king that your bishop supports.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.bispo.2: The king has no square: the queen covers f2, g2 and h1. Nobody can capture on f1: the knight on b1 blocks the rook on a1, and the rook on e2 blocks the bishop on d3.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.damaRei.1: Attack: back to White. With no other pieces, the queen's support comes from your king: on f7 it watches g7 and g8, next to the black king.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.damaRei.2: The queen goes to g7 and gives mate: the black king cannot capture it, because your king supports it, and it covers g8 and h7.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.damaRei.3: In the queen and king against king ending, mate usually comes like this: the black king on the edge, and the queen right next to it, supported by your king.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.excecao.1: Attack: the black rook on d2 attacks yours on e2, and the queen on b6 attacks your bishop on h6. Capturing the rook on d2 looks natural.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.excecao.p: Before capturing or defending, look for a check. Which move forces mate?
rot.queenRookMates.demos.excecao.certo: Yes, the check on e8. See why it forces mate.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.excecao.revela: The move is the rook check on e8, which forces mate, as you will see.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.excecao.err.e2d: The rook captures the one on d2, but the queen on b6 still attacks your bishop on h6.
With this move Black has a resource: the queen captures the bishop. Without it, the check on the eighth rank no longer mates, and the king escapes via g7.
Back to the position: look for the check that uses the bishop on h6 as support.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.excecao.err.h6e: The bishop escapes the queen's attack and blocks the diagonal of the bishop on c5, but your rook on e2 is still attacked.
With this move Black has a resource: the rook on d2 captures yours on e2, and your king is left without defence.
Back to the position: leave the bishop on h6 and look for the rook check.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.excecao.2: The king cannot go to g7, which the bishop on h6 watches. Black can only block.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.excecao.3: The bishop blocks on f8, the only move. There only the king defends it.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.excecao.4: The rook captures the bishop with mate: on f8 it stands next to the king, supported by the bishop on h6, and the king cannot capture it.
rot.queenRookMates.demos.excecao.5: In positions like this, the mate next to the king depends on the support: without the bishop on h6, the king would capture the rook on f8.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.valeAqui.enun: Back to White. The black king is on d7, and your rooks can give check. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.valeAqui.fim: On e7 the rook stood next to the king, supported by the pawn on d6, and closed the seventh rank. The king went back to d8, and the rook on a6 gave mate on a8: a ladder.
With the check on a7, the rook leaves the sixth rank, and the pawn on d6 loses its support: the black king captures it and escapes.
The rook attacks the queen, but without check and on a square the black queen attacks: it captures your rook.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.escadinha.enu: Back to White. The black king is on f8, on the eighth rank, and your rook on d7 occupies the seventh. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.escadinha.fim: The rook on a5 checked on a8, and the one on d7 closed the seventh rank: the king had no square. It is the ladder.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.escadinha.err: With the check on d8, the rook leaves the seventh rank, and the black king escapes along it.
Doubling the rooks on the seventh is not a check, and Black gains time: the king goes to e8 and attacks the rook on d7, which the one on a7 does not defend, because the pawn on b7 is in the way.
The rook on a5 leaves the a-file without check, and Black gains time: the king goes to e8 and attacks the rook on d7.
The rook captures the pawn on b7, but the rook on b3 recaptures.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.apoiada.enunc: Back to White. The black king is on h6, on the edge, and your pawn on g4 is close to it. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.apoiada.fim: The queen checked on h5, next to the king, supported by the pawn on g4. It covers g5, g6 and h7, and the king cannot capture it.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.apoiada.err.f: With the check on h7, the queen stands next to the king, but without support: the king captures it.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.apoiada.err.e: The rook goes to h3 without check, and Black gains time: the rook on g7 goes to g5 and attacks your queen.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.apoiada.err.f: The queen captures the pawn on f6 with check, but the queen on d8 recaptures.
rot.queenRookMates.pratica.apoiada.err.g: The pawn checks on g5, but the rook on g7 captures it, with check.
